sections.name: BaseAgent
sections.title: Shared behavior for every agent
sections.what: Defines the base agent that stores the database session and agent name, requires a run method, saves an audit record for each model call, and creates unique task identifiers.
sections.why: Gives every agent the same audit logging and identifier scheme without repeating code.
sections.watch_out: Each log call commits to the database immediately, so many calls in a row slow the agent down.

summary: Provides the shared starting point for every agent, including the record of each AI model call and a way to create unique task identifiers.
purpose: Makes every agent log its model calls the same way, which supports an audit trail.
why: Keeping logging in the base class means each agent gets it without repeating the code.
how: Each agent gives itself a name when it starts. Agents must write a run method. When an agent makes a model call, the base class saves a record with the provider, model, prompts, reply, tokens, timing, success flag and error. It also creates unique task identifiers from the agent name, time and a random part.
inputs: Provider name, model name, prompts, reply text, token counts, latency, task or survey identifiers, success flag, error text and extra metadata.
outputs: A saved audit record in the database and a new task identifier string.
risks: Full prompts and replies are stored, which may include sensitive survey content. If the audit model has a column named metadata, that name is reserved by the database library and can cause errors.
debug: If audit records are missing, check the database session and whether the commit runs. If a call fails to log, check the metadata and the field names on the audit model. If task identifiers look odd, check the agent name.
